sections.title: Mission · Choose the Right Operating System
paragraphs: Not every computer or workload needs the same operating system. Compare Windows, OS X/macOS, and Linux, and understand Linux distribution release and maintenance life cycles.
bullets: Differences between Windows, OS X/macOS, and Linux
sections.callout: MATCH THE OPERATING SYSTEM AND RELEASE MODEL TO THE NEED

sections.title: What Does an Operating System Do?
paragraphs: An operating system manages hardware, memory, processes, storage, devices, networking, and user interaction, while providing an environment for applications. Windows, macOS, and Linux perform these jobs but differ in licensing, ecosystem, configuration, hardware support, and administration.

sections.title: Microsoft Windows
paragraphs: Windows is Microsoft's operating-system ecosystem and is common on desktops and in organizations. It offers graphical tools and also supports command-line administration.

sections.title: OS X / macOS
paragraphs: OS X, now called macOS, is Apple's desktop operating-system ecosystem. It combines a graphical desktop with Unix-based command-line capabilities.

sections.title: Linux
paragraphs: Linux refers to operating systems built around the Linux kernel and distributed through many distributions. Linux can provide servers, desktops, embedded platforms, and cloud systems.

sections.title: Exam Trap · Linux Does Not Mean CLI Only
paragraphs: Linux can use a graphical desktop and a command line. Windows and macOS also provide command-line tools. Do not equate one operating system with only one interface.
sections.callout: LINUX ≠ CLI ONLY · WINDOWS/macOS ≠ GUI ONLY

sections.title: Desktop Configuration
paragraphs: Desktop environments and their settings control the graphical workspace, appearance, panels, menus, input, and other user-facing behavior. Linux distributions can offer different desktop choices.

sections.title: Distribution Life Cycles
paragraphs: A distribution life cycle describes how releases are developed, updated, supported, and eventually retired. Organizations consider support length before choosing a release.
sections.callout: LIFE CYCLE = HOW LONG IS IT MAINTAINED?

sections.title: Maintenance Cycles
paragraphs: A maintenance cycle defines the schedule and duration for fixes, security updates, and support. A stable release still needs ongoing maintenance.

sections.title: Beta Releases
paragraphs: A beta release is a pre-release intended for testing upcoming features and discovering problems. It may change and is not the usual production choice.

sections.title: Stable Releases
paragraphs: A stable release is intended for normal, reliable production use after testing. Stable does not mean maintenance has ended.
